summary: An excerpt from a fiction work (labeled Book 14, part 132) in which a narrator, who has been drinking wine, is alone with a man named Simon in an apartment. Simon is intoxicated, pressures her to keep drinking, listen to music and lie down, and grabs at her clothing and wrist. She dodges his advances, retreats to the bathroom, locks herself in, and becomes frightened as he calls to her and she considers the weak lock and the window that is too small to escape through. The narrator also notes a spy-camera shirt that is recording the scene.
one_line: A narrator fears for her safety after a drunken Simon pursues her in his apartment and she locks herself in the bathroom.
key_facts: The narrator says "I'm kinda drunk" and pretends to drink her wine, letting some slosh while wiping her mouth with her sleeve.
The narrator is wearing an expensive spy-camera shirt that is still recording everything in the room.
Simon crouches down to shuffle through albums and takes three tries to fit another one on the spindle.
Simon describes the album as coming from "Best band in the Twin Cities."
When Simon stands, he loses his balance and catches himself on the arm of the couch.
Simon's arm knocks against the wall when they tumble onto the bed.
Simon tries to push a hand down the back of the narrator's pants and reaches with clumsy hands to unbutton her shirt.
Simon grabs the narrator's wrist tight and asks, "Where you going?"
The narrator tells Simon she has to use the john again and says, "I'll be right back."
Simon kisses the narrator's knuckles romantically, but his words sound angry: "Don't be long."
The narrator locks herself in the little bathroom and sits on the toilet, shaking.
Simon calls out in a slurring sing-song voice, "Hey, getting lonely out here."
The narrator considers the bathroom door's lock to be flimsy and remembers how strong Simon's hands felt.
The bathroom window over the toilet is too small for her to escape through.
